body:
Request: groom a handful of drafts to Approved + drain mode so the overnight launcher has work — a concrete list, not "approve some"

RELAYED, unverifiable from your side: the operator asked whether you could approve drafts so the night keeps making progress. He is at the keyboard and wants steady throughput rather than an idle drain.

THE SITUATION. I started launcher v8 on batch night-0920 with FOUR drain-mode specs: BUG-1297, BUG-1298, BUG-1303, BUG-1420. That is roughly two hours of work. The launcher refreshes its batch every cycle — it scans for approved drain-mode specs and tags them in before counting — so anything you groom to Approved + drain is picked up automatically without either of us re-tagging. That is the fix for the followups-0918h failure, where a static batch went stale and sixteen approved specs sat invisible.

So the throughput question tonight is simply: is there approved drain-mode work. Right now, four.

WHAT I WOULD ASK YOU TO LOOK AT, and I have split the 24 drafts rather than handing you a pile.

SEVEN ARE AUTO-DRAFTED FAILURE RECORDS and I suspect most should be REJECTED rather than approved: BUG-1421, BUG-1296, BUG-1419, BUG-1315, BUG-1314, BUG-1313, BUG-1312. Each is "auto-complete failure: phase N on SPEC-X" for a spec that already exists and is already being worked. That is the same class as BUG-1318/1319/1320, which you rejected earlier — one of them was title-identical to a sibling. Clearing them shrinks the backlog the operator is trying to reduce without losing anything.

SIX LOOK LIKE GOOD DRAIN CANDIDATES — small, self-contained, one clear defect each:

  BUG-1305  `aida dev status` reports ACTIVE when the binary it points at does not exist
  BUG-1301  the portability ratchet blocks its own extension
  BUG-1316  a merge-hold burns the whole transient-retry budget and shelves as tool-exit
  BUG-1422  a batch of ineligible members relaunches forever; touched-nothing is indistinguishable from finished
  TASK-1298 the readiness check covers the substrate but not the machine
  BUG-1307  commits stranded on branches with no PR are reported nowhere

I would put BUG-1305 first if you take only one. It is the precise mechanism behind tonight's worst incident: the dev binary was deleted, `dev status` kept reporting ACTIVE, and a drain ran eight-day-old orchestration for twenty minutes while every health surface read normal. Fixing it means the next occurrence announces itself.

BUG-1307 is the least drain-ready of the six — it needs a decision about detection by patch-id versus trailer, and I wrote it as reporting rather than cleanup deliberately. If you would rather it stayed Draft until someone can think about it properly, that is the right call and I am not pushing.

THREE ARE LARGER and I am NOT asking you to approve them tonight: BUG-1418 and BUG-1423 are token/event telemetry and want SPIKE-83's report read first, which you just merged. STORY-1367 wants sequencing against STORY-1218 and that is a keyboard spec.

I have not touched any of them. Approval is your gate and this is a request, not a plan I have already started executing.
